explainer_content.short_definition: A 1960s songcraft lane where folk lyric weight, electric band sound, and vocal harmony become pop-rock language.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Folk-rock begins when folk songs and topical writing meet drums, electric guitars, and pop radio. Dylan, The Byrds, Simon & Garfunkel, Buffalo Springfield, and The Mamas & the Papas each balance seriousness and accessibility differently.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It expands what a pop-rock song can talk about. Protest, poetry, personal reflection, and generational unease can now sit beside hooks and harmonies.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: This lane is more lyric-centered than jangle pop alone and less studio-fantastical than psychedelic pop. The words and vocal blend carry as much weight as the guitars.
what_to_listen_for: Close harmonies that soften heavy lyrics
A rock backbeat under folk phrasing
